A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The complete main texts, Table 1, equations, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical convergence and classification-error results with proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Table 1 summarizes prior theoretical work.

after.justification: v3 remains a theoretical paper throughout the main text and Appendices A–D. Its added Bayes-error discussion does not report empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze the same fixed-width, two-layer leaky ReLU network with fixed second-layer weights and first-layer gradient descent on exponential loss. Correcting the notation for a_j does not alter the model already specified in v2.

E1.justification: Neither version reports empirical dataset or task coverage. The sub-Gaussian and polynomially tailed mixtures remain theoretical models; the added discussion of another paper does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Table 1 and Appendix A retain their theoretical comparisons; the added Karhadkar et al. citation is related-work discussion, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: No empirical evaluation protocols, splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures are introduced or revised. The stated gradient-descent conditions are theoretical assumptions.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies. Appendices A–D provide theoretical comparisons and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The probability-bound corrections concern mathematical reasoning, assessed under T1.

E6.justification: Neither version contains experimental scores, measured trends, or other concrete empirical result entries. Changes to analytical probability formulas belong to T1.

T1.justification: v3 changes κ(t) from P(|ξ1| ≥ t) to P(ξ1 ≥ t) in Theorem 5.1 and Lemma C.12, and restores a missing factor of one-half in C.12's proof. Theorem 4.8 also explicitly asserts uniqueness of problem (5), citing strict convexity. These are local revisions within the retained theorem and proof framework. Theorem C.13 still uses the old two-sided κ definition.

C1.justification: Despite the rewritten abstract, the central contributions remain directional convergence under gradient descent, benign overfitting beyond earlier distributional restrictions, a signal-strength phase transition, and failure conditions despite directional convergence. The introduction and discussion retain their substantive scope.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly relates the strong-signal isotropic Gaussian bounds to Bayes error, claiming optimality up to constants inside the Gaussian-tail argument. It also explicitly connects vanishing training loss to perfect interpolation. The discussion's limitations concerning label noise and more general networks remain.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hardware, runtimes, code or data access information are added or removed. The mathematical training specification is retained, apart from notation corrections.

R1.justification: v3 adds Karhadkar et al. (2024), distinguishing its hinge loss and label-flipping noise and relating its noise-free distribution to the strong-signal regime. It also adds Wainwright (2019) for the Gaussian Bayes-error formula. Existing comparisons in Table 1 and Appendix A remain.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract, restates the benign-overfitting definition in Section 3, moves the existing neuron-activation definition from Section 7 to Section 4, and adds acknowledgments and explanatory passages. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 restyles the title and author block, uses small-cap headings, adds running top rules, and reflows text and equations. Table 1 retains its structure and substantive contents; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Correcting the Gaussian-tail normalization and missing one-half factor improves mathematical accuracy, while the added explanations and references improve context. The gains are limited because the central results remain unchanged and Theorem C.13 still retains the conflicting two-sided κ definition, leaving the correction incompletely propagated.
